title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Ariana Clarke
content:
Purpose

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards for public APIs, code quality, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It includes the required decision records (ADRs) for major tradeoffs, ownership, and a lightweight compliance checklist used by architecture review and release gates. Use this page as the single source of truth for standards referenced during design reviews, pull requests, and operational runbooks.

Scope

Applies to all teams building or operating services and components that are part of Redwood Inference's production surface: hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments, and internal tooling. This document covers:
- API design and compatibility rules
- Coding standards and testing expectations
- Infrastructure and capacity practices
- Model-serving-specific constraints and configuration profiles
- Observability requirements and retention policies
- Performance SLOs and benchmarking guidance
- ADR process and a short ADR index

Quick summary (one-line per standard)

- API: Versioned, contract-first, JSON Schema + OpenAPI, idempotent mutations, stable error model.
- Code: Shared linting (prettier/eslint/clang-format), unit+integration test targets (>=90% for critical services), CI gating.
- Infra: IaC (Terraform) modules, immutable artifacts, environment parity (dev->staging->prod), and documented runbooks.
- Model-serving: Quantization profiles, kernel selection descriptors, KV cache TTLs, fallbacks for capacity.
- Observability: Structured logs, distributed traces, metrics with standardized labels, cost-aware sampling.
- Performance: Per-route P50/P95/P99 SLOs, token-cost budgets, continuous perf regression tests.

1) API Standards

Overview
Our API surface is the contract between customers and Redwood runtime. We must minimize breaking changes and provide clear upgrade paths. All outward-facing endpoints and internal RPCs follow the rules below.

Guidelines

- Spec: Publish an OpenAPI v3 spec (YAML/JSON) as part of each release. API changes require a spec diff in the PR.
- Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Breaking changes increment MAJOR. For hosted endpoints, we support pinned model routes and semantic versioning for handler behavior.
- Schema: Use JSON Schema for request/response validation. Include examples and edge-case tests.
- Error model: Use consistent error envelope {"error":{"code":"string","message":"string","details":{}}}. Document common codes (INVALID_INPUT, RATE_LIMIT, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE).
- Idempotency: All mutation endpoints must accept Idempotency-Key header and preserve idempotency for 72 hours.
- Pagination: Cursor-based (opaque cursor token).
- Rate limits: Tiered per-customer; responses must include X-RateLimit-* headers and returned Retry-After for 429.
- Streaming: Support server-sent events (SSE) or chunked transfer. Streaming contracts must be separately versioned.

API Checklist (required in PR)

1. OpenAPI spec included/updated.
2. Backwards-compatible change? If not, open ADR or deprecation timeline.
3. Request/response JSON Schema added and validated in tests.
4. Error codes documented.
5. Rate-limit headers present.

2) Coding Standards

Overview
Maintainable, readable, and testable code is a priority. We use language-specific style guides with shared expectations.

General rules

- Linters and formatters enabled in CI. No linter warnings admitted to main branch.
- Unit test coverage: service libraries >=70%, critical path libraries >=90%.
- Integration tests: API-level contract tests against a local stack or mocked runtime.
- Type safety: Prefer static typing (TypeScript, mypy, or equivalent).
- Secrets: Never checked into source; use vault/KMS.
- Dependency updates: automated via Dependabot or Renovate; major upgrades require regression run.

PR Requirements

- Small, focused PRs (<400 lines where practical).
- Describe design and performance impact in PR description.
- Add changelog entry for public API-affecting PRs.

3) Infrastructure Standards

IaC and environments

- All infra managed in Terraform modules stored in git. Modules have stable interfaces and are reviewed by infra owners.
- Environments: dev, staging (pre-prod), prod. Staging mirrors prod network and capacity ratios.
- Artifacts: Build artifacts are immutable and versioned. Deployment uses artifact tags.

Network, security, and secrets

- VPC design: regional subnets per availability zone, private control plane for Private deployments.
- KMS/HSM integration required for customer-managed keys.
- RBAC: least privilege for service accounts.

Capacity and autoscaling

- Dedicated GPU pools: reserved capacity with autoscaling policies and safety buffer (20% headroom) to preserve SLOs.
- Warm pools and cold-start mitigation for model-serving endpoints.

Table: Infra minimal requirements

| Component | Minimum prod config | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control plane | 3 x t3.medium (HA) | Single region control plane supported for Private deployments
| Serving pool (GPU) | 2x A10G per shard | Shard counts depend on model latency profile
| Metrics retention | 90 days (full), 365 days (aggregates) | Cost/retention tradeoff for long term analysis

4) Model-serving Standards

Profiles and packaging

- Model Profiles: Each model must have a JSON profile (model-id, arch, tokenizer-version, max-seq, quantization-options, kernel-hints). Profiles are validated on onboarding.
- Quantization: Approved quantization profiles (int8, int4) listed in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Use recommended profiles per model family.
- KV cache: Default TTL 120s for shared caches, configurable per-customer. Cache invalidation must be documented for deployments that serve multi-tenant workloads.

Runtime behavior

- Kernel selection: Runtime will pick kernels per profile; if custom kernels are required, add an ADR.
- Fallbacks: Policy-based fallbacks to compatible model variants (e.g., smaller quantized model) when capacity constrained. Fallbacks must preserve the same response schema.

Onboarding checklist

1. Model profile JSON added to model-catalog.
2. Perf benchmark (P50/P95/P99 token latency) under standard load.
3. Quality evals: prompt-set results and regression thresholds.
4. Quantization and correctness validation.

5) Observability Standards

Metrics

- Metric naming: snake_case, dot-separated service prefix, e.g., runtime.request.latency_ms. All metrics must include labels: service, route, model_id, region, env.
- SLO metrics: request_count, error_count, latency_histogram.

Logging

- Structured JSON logs with these fields: timestamp, level, service, request_id, trace_id, user_id (if available), model_id, message, meta.
- PII: never log raw customer input. Redact or hash identifiers per data-retention policy.

Tracing

- Distributed tracing enabled for all services (OpenTelemetry). Traces should capture key spans: request ingress, model scheduling, GPU kernel invocation, response serialization.
- Sampling: 100% for high-error-rate traces, adaptive sampling for low-latency traces (default 5%).

Alerting and Dashboards

- Standard dashboards per service: traffic, latency (P50/P95/P99), errors, resource utilization.
- Paging thresholds managed by eng-sre; critical alerts must include a playbook link.

Retention Policies

- Logs: 30 days full, 365 days aggregates/indices.
- Traces: 15 days full, 90 days sampled.
- Metrics: 90 days full resolution, 365 days rolled-up.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarks

SLOs (baseline public SLOs)

- Text generation API (hosted)
  - P50 <= 50ms (token generation, per-token)
  - P95 <= 250ms (per-request end-to-end for typical 64-token request)
  - Error rate <= 0.1% (5xx errors)

- Embeddings API
  - P95 <= 200ms per request
  - Error rate <= 0.05%

Throughput and cost control

- Batch sizing: recommend dynamic batching heuristics; batch size ceilings per model profile documented in profile JSON.
- Unit-cost targets: set per-model token cost budgets; SRE monitors overages and notifies on +15% deviation.

Performance testing

- CI-perf: synthetic perf tests run nightly for critical routes. Regression >5% triggers triage.
- Canary testing: deploy to canary fleet with 5-10% traffic and run end-to-end perf comparison before global rollout.

7) ADR (Architecture Decision Record) Process and Index

Process

1. New architecture decisions affecting cross-team behavior must be recorded as ADRs. Use ADR template in /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-template.
2. Draft ADR and submit for review to listed reviewers. If the decision affects SLOs, include eng-sre and product.
3. ADR review window: 5 business days. Emergency ADRs can be fast-tracked with approver sign-off recorded in the ADR.

ADR metadata required

- Title, status (proposed|accepted|deprecated), date, authors, reviewers, related services, summary, consequences, rollback.

Short ADR index (examples)

- ADR-2025-11: "Model Quantization Strategy" — adopted int8 default with int4 optional for low-memory GPUs.
- ADR-2026-01: "API Versioning and Deprecation Policy" — semantic versioning + 90-day deprecation window for minor changes.
- ADR-2026-03: "Fallback Routing Policy" — policies and priority order for model fallbacks and regional routing.

8) Ownership, Review, and Enforcement

- Standards owner: Arch & Standards guild (rotating chairs). Day-to-day custodian: eng-platform.
- Review: Architecture review required for changes that touch multiple services, alter SLOs, or change customer-visible APIs.
- Enforcement: CI gates, architecture review sign-off, and SRE verification for prod rollout. Non-compliant rollouts can be blocked by infra or SRE.

9) Templates and Checklists (links)

- ADR Template: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-template
- API PR Checklist: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/api-pr-checklist
- Model Onboarding Checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/checklist

10) References

- Runtime architecture: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture-2026-03-01
- SLO and error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2026-02-15
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles

Appendix A — Common configurations (table)

| Setting | Recommended value | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default KV cache TTL | 120s | Balances cost and latency for repeated prefixes |
| Idempotency window | 72h | Matches typical retry windows for SDKs |
| Logs retention (full) | 30 days | Supports incident triage without excessive cost |
| Traces sampling | 5% baseline | Keeps storage manageable while preserving triage ability |

Appendix B — Example ADR (short)

- ADR-2026-03: Fallback Routing Policy
  - Status: accepted
  - Authors: Ariana Clarke, Samir Patel
  - Summary: Runtime should attempt (1) same-model degraded-quantized variant, (2) smaller model family with same schema, (3) regional fallback, in that order.
  - Consequences: Slightly higher latency for degraded responses and careful rollout required to ensure quality.

Questions or exceptions

Open an architecture review ticket or contact the Arch & Standards guild (arch-standards@redwood-inference.internal). For urgent production issues, contact eng-sre on-call and follow incident playbook at /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.
